title: NVIDIA's Rubin Hits Mass Production in Q3 as Diamond-Copper Enters Platform Spec
body: In the third quarter of 2026, the first mass-production Vera Rubin NVL72 AI server rack rolled off the automated production line of Ingrasys, a Foxconn subsidiary, and shipped to Microsoft. NVIDIA confirmed on its May earnings call that Rubin would begin shipping in Q3, with every rack built on a diamond-copper composite material paired with 45°C warm-water direct liquid cooling; the CFO guided that Rubin would contribute roughly 20% of data-center revenue, while supply could cover only about 70% of demand.

Diamond-copper — a diamond/copper composite — delivers 600–800 W/(m·K) thermal conductivity, roughly double pure copper's ~400 W/(m·K), while staying compatible with existing skiving and brazing processes. It has now been written into the platform specification. Analyst reports cited by the article put Rubin's rack TDP at up to 2300W versus 700W for H100, with hotspot pressure reaching 770 W/cm².

On the supply chain, Taiwan ODMs locked in full-rack integration: Quanta, Wistron and Foxconn moved into volume conversion in Q3, with Foxconn guiding full ramp-up from Q4, though analysts estimate over 95% of Q3 racks shipped were still GB300. Jentech won the initial vapor-chamber supply for Rubin, with per-unit pricing stepping from about $30 in the Blackwell Ultra generation to ~$100 for Rubin and ~$200 for Rubin Ultra. On the Chinese materials side, Sifangda (planning CNY 450 million for a 25,000-piece-per-year 4-inch line), Guoji Jinggong and Worldia (CNY 520 million expansion) are all in qualification.

title: SK Hynix Pauses Solidigm US IPO Review, Shelving Potential $15 Billion Raise
body: SK Hynix announced on October 23 that it has suspended its review of a US IPO for its American subsidiary Solidigm, citing heightened financial-market volatility and weak semiconductor stocks, and stressed the move does not reflect any change in Solidigm's growth outlook or investment needs.

Reuters reported on September 25 that Solidigm had held an IPO underwriter bake-off, with a listing as early as 2027 at a valuation of up to $150 billion — which would set a US semiconductor IPO record — raising as much as $15 billion to fund new US production facilities. The halt stems from two pressures: market volatility, and tightening Korean oversight. SK Hynix's own shares have fallen more than 30% since late September (KOSPI down 20%) on dilution concerns, while regulators warned the listing may fall under Korea's tightened dual-listing rules.

Solidigm, based in Rancho Cordova, California, makes NAND flash and enterprise SSDs. It was born from SK Hynix's 2020 acquisition of Intel's NAND and storage business for about $9 billion, completed in two phases in March 2025. Its enterprise SSDs reach 122.88TB and serve AI data-center servers and cloud infrastructure; H1 2026 revenue was KRW 12.25 trillion, up 265% year-on-year, with net profit of KRW 5.84 trillion.

title: US Commerce Plans Up to $389 Million for Power-Semiconductor R&D, GaN Targets AI Data-Center Power Bottleneck
body: On October 22, the US Department of Commerce announced plans to provide up to $389 million in research funding to four companies for power-semiconductor devices and key materials, under the $10 billion semiconductor R&D program in the 2022 CHIPS and Science Act; it is the program's 20th award in recent months.

The four recipients: Helion (up to $175 million) for high-voltage power semiconductors and advanced energy power modules for fusion power, with a $50 million private-investment match and a production line in Everett, Washington in partnership with GlobalFoundries; Commonwealth Fusion Systems ($85 million) for RF plasma heating and power-electronics semiconductors; Vertical Semiconductor ($73 million) for vertical-structure GaN power semiconductors aimed at AI data-center racks, including a 2.5-megawatt rack demonstration; and Sibelco North America ($56 million) for next-generation ultra-high-purity quartz purification and a demonstration facility in North Carolina.

GaN is positioned as a fix for the AI power crisis: next-generation AI processors will draw 2–4 kW per chip and rack power is pushing past 1 MW, making power delivery and conversion efficiency a core bottleneck. A condition of the awards is that the government takes a minority, non-voting equity stake — for example, $175 million of Helion's latest Series G preferred shares.

title: BYD Semiconductor Ships 50M+ Units of BF1190/1186 Automotive Isolation Gate-Driver Series
body: BYD Semiconductor has brought its BF1190/BF1186 series of automotive-grade isolated gate drivers into full mass production, with cumulative shipments of this type exceeding 50 million units across automotive and industrial markets.

The BF1190 is a single-channel driver with CMTI above 150 kV/μs, integrating primary/secondary undervoltage protection, desaturation protection, Miller clamp and soft turn-off. The BF1186-F is a dual-channel part with CMTI above 100 kV/μs and integrated Miller clamp. Both deliver up to ±10A drive current and at least 5.7 kVrms isolation, meeting AEC-Q100 automotive standards, and drive IGBT and SiC power devices directly without extra buffers or driver amplifiers.
Target applications cover automotive main drives, OBC/DCDC, air-compressor and PTC heaters, plus industrial PV and energy-storage inverters and AI server power supplies.

title: Leadmicro's Yuanchuang Precision Hits Dual-Route MFC Mass Production for Domestic Substitution
body: Yuanchuang Precision, under Guangdong Lead Group, has brought both of its mass flow controller (MFC) technology routes — thermal and differential-pressure — into volume production, becoming one of the few domestic makers with both routes scaled and multiple customers qualified. MFCs, called the 'nerve valves' of semiconductor process gas lines, require 6–12 units per etcher chamber.

The differential-pressure VG80 targets precision small-flow control for etchers, while the PG90 covers a wider flow range for ALD/CVD tools; the new thermal T90 product uses proven VG-series piezoelectric technology. Together the two routes cover over 90% of semiconductor process scenarios.

The push sits within Lead Group's components-platform strategy, showcased at the October 14–16 Bay Area Semiconductor Industry Eco Expo in Shenzhen. Founded in 1995, Lead Group reported 2025 revenue exceeding CNY 47 billion; its Shanghai base is expected to be completed in 2027.

GaN power devices are penetrating the robotics sector at an accelerating pace. On October 15, ZHUOYU Technology announced a bulk purchase order for 100,000 planetary joint modules from a national-level customer, with a contract value exceeding CNY 100 million. The modules integrate GaN power devices at the drive end, cutting conduction and switching losses and achieving over 95% drive efficiency, and ZHUOYU plans to scale joint-module capacity to 2 million units by 2027 and 10 million units by 2028.

On October 13, InnoScience announced a co-development partnership with Ulink Intelligent on GaN-based joint modules, using three-phase full-bridge topology plus half-bridge bootstrap drive with low-voltage GaN devices, cutting power-conversion losses by 50%, shrinking the main power-conversion circuit by 75% and the whole machine by 15-20%. InnoScience's H1 2026 report disclosed 465,000 GaN chips delivered to the humanoid-robotics market, up 50% year-on-year, with adoption expanding into joint drives, 48V/12V power conversion, BMS, dexterous hands and LiDAR.

Infineon introduced a 100V GaN motor-drive reference design that packs GaN devices and a leadless QFN package directly inside the motor body, targeting humanoid and mobile-robotics applications. The company projects 300 million humanoid robots by 2050 with an average BOM cost of about $500 each including Si/GaN power semiconductors and DC-DC converters. Researchers estimate the GaN-for-humanoid-robotics market will reach CNY 347 million by 2031 at a 2026-2031 CAGR of 90.04%.
title: GaN Gains Ground in Robotics: ZHUOYU Lands 100K Joint-Module Order, InnoScience and Infineon Push Ahead

body: Canon plans to raise the production capacity of its semiconductor back-end lithography equipment to 150% of 2026 levels by 2029, a 50% increase, Japan's Nikkan Kogyo Shimbun reported on October 20. The expansion will come from ramping up the new factory at its Utsunomiya site, improving production efficiency, and developing products for large substrates.

In a January interview, Canon executive officer Yoaki Takeishi said Canon built a new plant in Utsunomiya, Tochigi, in 2025, lifting semiconductor lithography equipment capacity to 1.5 times the 2024 level; the new plant started operation in September 2025 and targets full production in 2027.

Canon's back-end tools support 510 x 515 mm substrates with high alignment accuracy, a wide exposure field and 0.8-micron resolution, delivering a 52 x 68 mm single-shot field stitched to 100 x 100 mm exposure in four shots, with distortion aberration cut to less than one-quarter of the previous generation. Canon expects to ship 69 KrF and 169 i-line lithography tools in 2026, 238 in total, up four units year-on-year. On October 13, 2023, Canon launched its new-generation nanoimprint lithography tool, becoming the first vendor to commercialize nanoimprint semiconductor manufacturing equipment with 14 nm minimum line width, and delivered the system to the Texas Institute for Electronics on September 26, 2024.
title: Canon to Raise Back-End Lithography Equipment Capacity 50% by 2029

body: On October 19 local time, the U.S. State Department sanctioned five Chinese entities under the Protecting American Intellectual Property Act, citing 'trade secret theft.' The five entities are Shanghai Zhisuan Technology Co., Ltd., MiraclePlus (formerly Y Combinator China), three venture-capital funds linked to MiraclePlus, and one management entity affiliated with it.

Shanghai Zhisuan Technology is an AI infrastructure developer founded in 2023; its founder Linwei Ding was convicted in the U.S. for allegedly stealing Google AI trade secrets. The sanctions reach up the capital chain, targeting the incubator and the seed-round funds alongside the accused company itself. Specific restrictive measures have not yet been disclosed.

On the same day, the U.S. Department of Homeland Security issued a rule requiring all federal civilian agencies to remove all DeepSeek products and derivatives from their IT systems and banning further procurement. On October 20, China's Ministry of Commerce responded with a four-point statement: condemning the sanctions as 'vile' and 'firmly opposed,' stating that China's AI development has nothing to do with the alleged trade-secret theft, urging the U.S. to correct its actions, and warning it will take 'necessary measures' in response.
title: U.S. Sanctions Five Chinese Entities Over Alleged Trade-Secret Theft, DHS Bans DeepSeek From Federal IT

body: Hunan Goke Microelectronics notified customers and distributors on October 22 of a new round of price increases on packaged KGD (Known Good Die) storage products effective November 2026. It is Goke's second hike this year, and the first quoted as absolute dollar amounts rather than percentage increases.

Under the notice, packaged 64MB KGD rises by $0.50, 128MB by $1.00, and 256MB by $1.50; products with external DDR will be notified separately. The stated reason is the industry-wide DDR shortage and rising market prices widening the supply gap, with substrate and lead-frame material costs also climbing sharply. In January 2026, Goke raised packaged 512Mb, 1Gb and 2Gb KGD by 40%, 60% and 80% respectively using percentage terms.

TrendForce data shows Q4 2026 conventional DRAM contract prices are expected to rise 10-15% quarter-on-quarter, PC DRAM 13-18%, and NAND Flash 15-20%. Packaged KGD, which integrates a controller and tested DRAM dies in one package, is widely used in surveillance, automotive electronics, industrial control, edge AI and IoT devices, where downstream customers have little room to pause purchases.
title: Goke Micro Raises Packaged KGD Storage Prices a Second Time This Year

body: NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang told CNBC on October 22 during the GTC Berlin conference that despite the past week's sharp selloff in memory stocks on oversupply fears, he does not see memory oversupply emerging through 2029. 'The good thing about memory is you can always use more,' he said, noting that HBM will keep being used for many years to come.

Asked whether NVIDIA would work with China's CXMT and adopt its memory products, Huang said 'we're open,' adding that 'almost every company in the world works with a Chinese company somewhere in their supply chain.' He praised China's manufacturing prowess and acknowledged that U.S. export controls have accelerated China's semiconductor development: 'No doubt, we accelerated all of this.'

The selloff was triggered by CXMT president Cao Kan Yu's October 10 announcement of key progress on 4F² DRAM architecture, targeting DDR5 RDIMM server memory products by the end of 2026. TrendForce data shows CXMT's global DRAM revenue share reached about 9.5% in Q2 2026, ranking fourth worldwide. Micron dismissed 4F² as lacking a viable path to scale after more than two decades of exploration, while Samsung confirmed it is developing a 4F² VCT architecture expected to reach commercial production around 2028.
title: Jensen Huang Sees No Memory Oversupply Through 2029, Open to Working With CXMT
Micron Dismisses 4F² DRAM as CXMT Advances VSG Transistor, Eyes Server DDR5 RDIMM
body: ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) has made key progress on its next-generation 4F² DRAM cell architecture and plans to launch server-grade DDR5 RDIMM products combining the 4F² architecture with hybrid-bonding technology before the end of 2026.

At its October 21, 2026 technology webinar, Micron took the opposite view: after more than two decades of exploration, 4F² DRAM has no feasible scaling path due to complexity and cost. Micron is abandoning the 4F² route, extending the advantages of its 6F² architecture and making 3D DRAM its future direction.

CXMT's 4F² architecture uses a self-developed vertical surrounding-gate (VSG) transistor, shrinking cell footprint by about one third and lifting theoretical storage density by about 50%. Founded in 2016 and headquartered in Hefei, CXMT has grown its global DRAM revenue share from around 4% to about 10%, according to HSBC data.

Micron's node roadmap: 1γ is in high-volume production with first EUV use; 1δ (seventh-generation 10nm-class DRAM) is ramping for volume in the second half of 2027 — the first node manufactured in the US — delivering about 25% generational density gain over 1γ; 1ε introduces wafer bonding; the ζÅ (Zeta-Angstrom) first sub-10nm-class node is in early development with High-NA EUV; 3D DRAM will evolve through 3D1 and 3D2 nodes.

title: NVIDIA Signs Six Suppliers to Massive Capacity Expansion at GTC Berlin
body: On October 21, 2026, the opening day of GTC Berlin, NVIDIA announced large-scale capacity expansion agreements with six suppliers — Amkor, Ibiden, KYEC, Samsung Electro-Mechanics, SPIL and Unimicron — spanning substrates, advanced packaging, semiconductor testing and optical engines.

Substrates: product substrate capacity will rise 2.5x within three years; NVIDIA is paying Ibiden billions of dollars in capacity-reservation prepayments to expand its Ohno plant toward triple current levels; Samsung Electro-Mechanics joins as a new member, contributing its Korean line capacity immediately while upgrading and building its Sejong and Busan plants.

Advanced packaging: with Amkor, Korea interposer wafer capacity is set to rise more than 300% by end-2028; Amkor signed a new $1.3 billion agreement the same day, bringing its NVIDIA-related agreements to $3 billion.
Testing: total test capacity is expected to double during 2026-2027; NVIDIA is paying KYEC an $1.1 billion prepayment for a new US test facility targeting mass production in April 2027.
Optical engines: with SPIL, Taiwan optical-engine capacity is targeted at 15x current levels by mid-2027 and doubling again by end-2028.

title: DeepSeek Deepens Huawei Ties, Plans Pre-Training on Ascend 950DT by Year-End
body: The Information reported on October 20, citing sources, that DeepSeek is working closely with Huawei and participating in design decisions for future Huawei AI chips; Huawei is adjusting chip designs to DeepSeek's requirements on model computation and inter-processor data transfer, with the resulting designs feeding AI chips launching in 2027 and beyond.

DeepSeek plans to begin AI model pre-training on Huawei's Ascend 950DT as early as year-end, with latest tests already using over 1,000 processors — the timeline subject to test progress. Huawei plans to prioritize most of the supply of the Ascend 960DT, launching in Q1 2027, for DeepSeek, for both training and inference.

DeepSeek has open-sourced TileLang compiler tools and compute/communication components for the Ascend platform (TileLang was developed by Peking University researchers), releasing a version supporting the Ascend 950 on September 30. IDC data shows NVIDIA's share of China's datacenter AI-chip market fell to 34% in the first half of 2026, with Huawei at 28% — the gap narrowed to six percentage points.

title: Alibaba's T-Head Unveils Automotive-Grade XuanTie E908A, Maps Out Full RISC-V Ecosystem Push
body: Alibaba's T-Head (DAMO Academy) released the XuanTie E908A, a new automotive-grade-enhanced processor built on the E908 platform, billed as the first processor to simultaneously reach ASIL-B/ASIL-D levels, with performance leading contemporary rivals by 20% and single-point fault metric (SPFM) exceeding 90% for the first time in the industry. It provides a real-time compute foundation for safety islands, domain controllers and in-vehicle gateways.

The roadmap calls for C925A, C930A and C950A to follow, with the C950A expected to deliver 5x the combined performance of the first generation; server products based on the newest XuanTie 950 are expected to appear next year, and T-Head projects single-core multi-threaded SPECint2026 to surpass 100 points by 2028.

On the hardware-ecosystem side, the new XT-LINK high-performance multi-core interconnect keeps XuanTie C950 efficiency at about 78% with 128 cores; for four agentic-AI workload scenarios, multi-core XuanTie C950 systems lead x86 rivals by about 11%, while joint SMT exploration with ZTE Microelectronics delivers a 35% performance gain on SMT2 (C950).

The AI-native XPU architecture natively supports scalar, vector and matrix (tensor) compute with typical operator utilization above 80%, multi-level memory (SRAM-system cache-DDR) with bandwidth utilization above 90%, and Transformer-targeted SFU hotspot acceleration that improves Softmax, Norm and RoPE operators by 2-10x — with Qwen3.8-Flash-Next inference reaching 43 tokens per second.

Software contributions are piling up: 43 GCC patches (17.5% community share, second only to Qualcomm's 34.6%, worth about 10% typical performance gain), 111 LLVM patches (+20% versus community LLVM), and 48 OpenJDK patches with the Chinese Academy of Sciences' Institute of Software (56.47% share, +31% SPECjbb on the C950). A 20-board A210 cloud cluster now runs daily AOSP builds and CTS/VTS regression tests, and commercial OS editions are shipping with Ubuntu, Alibaba Cloud and Kylinsoft.

title: Shenzhen Packaging-Equipment 'Little Giant' Weijian Files for IPO Tutoring
body: Shenzhen Weijian Advanced Packaging Technology Co., founded in December 2019 by chairman Lei Weizhuang, completed IPO tutoring registration with the Shenzhen securities regulator on October 19, with Huatai United Securities as the tutoring broker. It remains at the tutoring stage, with no audited financial data disclosed and no listing venue named.

The national-level 'little giant' SME builds advanced packaging equipment: storage-chip packaging gear such as the MV-M50, capable of 16-layer stacking for HBM-class high-density memory, and optical-transceiver packaging equipment including couplers supporting dual-lens, dual-FA, CPO lens and FAU coupling, plus 1.5-micron high-precision die bonders and TCB equipment.

Business is surging: first-half sales of storage packaging equipment grew more than 500% year on year and optical-transmission packaging equipment more than 300%; the company serves seven to eight of the world's top ten optical device and module makers, with overseas orders accounting for more than 20% of the total.

In May it expanded its manufacturing headquarters to over 20,000 square meters, lifting annual capacity past 3,000 units with one-to-three-month delivery on standard models, and a second round of capacity expansion is underway.

Funding history runs one round per year: Pre-A in August 2021 (tens of millions, led by SMIC Juyuan), A in April 2022 (tens of millions, led by BaseStone Capital), A+ in October 2023 (near RMB 100 million, led by Haitong Kaiyuan), A++ in January 2024, and B in August 2025 (over RMB 100 million). There is no controlling shareholder; the three founders controlled 65.72% of voting rights as of end-June.

title: Tianyue Advanced Swings to Profit as 8-Inch SiC Substrates Top 50% of Revenue
body: China's Tianyue Advanced reported first-nine-months revenue of RMB 1.559 billion, up 40.22% year on year to a record high, with net profit of RMB 27.22 million — up 2,330.24% year on year. The third quarter alone delivered RMB 646 million in revenue and RMB 85.83 million in net profit, erasing a roughly RMB 58.6 million first-half loss; Q3 gross margin recovered to 27.46%.

Revenue from 8-inch SiC substrates passed 50% of the total, which the report notes puts the domestic maker on the same starting line as global leaders — a step from being able to make large wafers to making them at scale and at low cost.

The company attributes the inflection to rising 800V EV-platform penetration driving automotive-grade conductive substrates, with AI-server high-voltage power emerging as a second growth engine alongside PV/energy storage and ultra-fast charging. Net margin remains thin at about 1.75%, and capex stays heavy: operating cash flow was RMB 89 million while investing outflows exceeded RMB 2.6 billion.

title: Xinde Semiconductor Clears HKEX Hearing, Eyes Advanced-Packaging Expansion
body: Hong Kong's stock exchange disclosed on October 21 that Jiangsu Xinde Semiconductor Technology has passed its listing hearing. The OSAT firm develops packaging design, custom packaging products and testing services through its "CAPiC" platform, spanning QFN, BGA, LGA, WLP and 2.5D/3D.
IPO proceeds will fund a new production base and lines, advanced-packaging R&D — specifically LDFO, X-SiP, TXV and 2.5D/3D integration — plus commercialization and customer-ecosystem expansion.

Revenue rose from RMB 509.1 million in 2023 to RMB 827.4 million in 2024 and RMB 1.012 billion in 2025, while the gross loss margin improved from 38.4% to 18.0%. The company holds 225 patents in China, including 39 invention patents, plus three PCT applications.

title: Resistor Supply Tightens: YAGEO, Walsin Hiked Prices 15–20%, Lead Times Stretch
body: Current-sense resistors are being repriced from supporting parts to system-critical components as a passive-components shortage cycle takes hold. YAGEO raised prices on key resistor series by 15–20% and Walsin raised its full resistor lineup by about 20% in February 2026, citing elevated silver, palladium, ruthenium, tin and copper costs; smaller makers followed with 5–20% increases.

Lead times for high-end parts have stretched: YAGEO resistors sit around 24 weeks and Samsung Electro-Mechanics around 44 weeks, versus about 10 weeks for ROHM on its IDM supply; new capacity is slow to release as line construction and customer qualification cycles are long.

Demand tracks electrification and higher power: NEV battery management, onboard chargers and inverters, industrial servo and drives, and — the fastest-growing segment — AI/data-center server power supplies chasing higher power density and smaller packages.

title: Jieyang Micro's GT1500 UWB Chip Passes FiRa Core 4.0 Certification
body: Shenzhen Jieyang Micro's GT1500-series UWB chips have passed the FiRa Consortium's FiRa Core 4.0 certification, the international body's latest and most demanding UWB wireless standard, covering multi-protocol compatibility, automotive-grade security and high-precision ranging.

The series supports CCC digital-key standards for automotive use — high-precision smart entry, secure unlock and find-my-car — plus the Aliro access standard for contactless building and transit gates with millisecond-level secure checks.

The chips integrate financial-grade security with preset secure timestamping (STS) against relay attacks, and support angle-of-arrival measurement with centimeter-level ranging and multi-target coordination. Jieyang positions them for physical AI and edge AI — robots, robot dogs and warehouse AGVs needing reliable indoor positioning.

title: SmartSens Launches SC2150 Image Sensor with 12μm Pixels for Security
body: SmartSens (688213) has launched the SC2150, a CMOS image sensor for high-end smart-security applications built on its SmartClarity-3 platform, with a large-format sensor and 12μm pixels targeting long-range telephoto scenes in low light.

It uses PixGain HDR and dual-exposure staggered SHDR to reach up to 100dB dynamic range. Sensitivity is rated at 67,146 mV/lux·s with SNR1 of 0.012 lux; quantum efficiency hits 83% in visible light and 54%/42% at 850nm/940nm — up 58% and 29% over its predecessor.

Target applications include electronic astronomical telescopes, maritime cargo monitoring, forest-fire prevention and wildlife protection, in monochrome and color versions. Sampling is open now, with mass production targeted for Q1 2027.

title: Tenstorrent Closes $1.5 Billion Series E at $6.2 Billion Valuation
body: US AI-chip unicorn Tenstorrent has closed a $1.5 billion Series E round at a $6.2 billion post-money valuation, led by Trace Capital and Innovation X, with participation from Fidelity, ARK Invest, Morgan Stanley, Cadence Ventures, Eclipse, Sandisk, T. Rowe Price, Tether Investments, Virtu Financial, XTX Markets and the Agostinelli Group.
The Santa Clara company, founded in 2016 and led by CEO Jim Keller, says the capital will fund scaled deployment of its Galaxy rack servers and expansion of its AI and CPU IP licensing business.
Tenstorrent builds RISC-V-based AI processors and licenses RISC-V CPU IP (TT-Ascalon) and AI core IP (Tensix), counting Samsung and LG Electronics as IP customers.

Its hardware has evolved from the 12nm Grayskull card to Wormhole, which carries 128 Tensix cores, GDDR6 memory and 488 TFLOPS of FP16 compute per card, with direct Ethernet inter-chip links that move data without going through the host CPU.
The round follows a $200M-plus Series C in May 2021 that valued the company at $1 billion, and a $693M-plus Series D in December 2024 led by Samsung Securities and AFW Partners.

title: ZTE Micro Unveils 'Everest 200' RISC-V CPU for AI Data Centers
body: ZTE Microelectronics unveiled its first high-performance RISC-V CPU for AI data centers, the 'Everest 200' (珠峰200), at the 2026 RISC-V China Summit in Shenzhen on October 19.

The chip follows the RVA23 profile and pairs a 64-bit superscalar out-of-order core with native AI acceleration — large vector and matrix units, KV-cache optimization, and hardware engines for retrieval, reranking, compression and encryption — targeting trillion-parameter MoE models.

It supports top-tier DDR5 memory with DDR MRDIMM expansion, PCIe 6.0 and CXL 3, and is positioned for three use cases: high-density Agent CPU clusters, host CPUs in inference supernodes paired with GPU and accelerator clusters, and enterprise hybrid-inference appliances.
ZTE Micro did not disclose detailed specifications at the event and expects a formal launch by the end of this year.

title: Spacemit Launches 46-Core V100, Billed as First Fully RISC-V-Server-Spec-Compliant Chip
body: Chinese RISC-V vendor Spacemit (进迭时空) has unveiled its first server-grade RISC-V chip, the V100, described as the first compute chip fully compliant with the RISC-V server specification, at the 2026 RISC-V China Summit.

The V100 integrates 46 RISC-V cores — six high-performance Kunming Lake V2R2 cores from the OpenHW 'Xiangshan' project plus 40 of Spacemit's own X100 efficiency cores — and can scale to 92 cores through dual-socket coherent interconnect.

It supports 8-channel DDR5 at 4800MT/s with 307GB/s of bandwidth and up to 2TB per socket, plus 52 PCIe 5.0 lanes that can host eight AI accelerators; the Kunming Lake cores are built on 7nm, run at up to 3GHz and score 15 on SPECINT2006 per GHz, positioned against Arm's Neoverse N2.

The chip covers all five pillars of the RISC-V server specification — the RVA23 profile, Server SoC, Server Platform, Boot and Runtime Services, and the security model — passing the full BRS test suite and booting mainstream Linux distributions including Ubuntu, Debian, Fedora and Red Hat.

Spacemit also launched three server systems, with the G5201 AI server supporting eight dual-width accelerator cards and demonstrated running domestic Kunlunxin M100 accelerators and the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash model.

title: Groq Bets on 3D-Stacked DRAM for Next-Gen AI Chips, Moving Off SRAM
body: Groq, the SRAM-centric AI chip company recently acquired in substance by Nvidia, is reportedly evaluating 3D-stacked DRAM packaging for its next-generation chips to break through the capacity ceiling of traditional SRAM.

The scheme, dubbed 3DS, uses TSV (through-silicon via) technology to punch thousands of vertical micro-vias through DRAM dies, stacking them like a skyscraper to deliver ultra-high memory density per unit area.

Unlike the HBM used in Nvidia's high-end GPUs, which chases extreme data rates, 3DS keeps the standard DRAM interface protocol and prioritizes capacity expansion — a more pragmatic cost-efficiency play for AI inference workloads that must load massive parameter sets.

Groq's LPU architecture is famed for its inference speed but relies on tiny SRAM pools that strain under hundred-billion-parameter models; stacked DRAM aims to preserve the speed edge while solving the 'doesn't fit' problem.

title: Samsung Shifts M2800 Modem to 2nm, Frees 4nm Capacity for HBM4 Base Die
body: Samsung is reallocating advanced-node capacity: its next-generation mobile modem, the M2800, will move to a 2nm process, freeing up 4nm capacity for HBM base dies — the control-function chips at the bottom of HBM stacks.
According to The Elec, Samsung System LSI expects to complete development of the M2800 in 2027; the modem will pair with the Exynos 2800 in the Galaxy S28 series slated for 2028.

Industry sources say more than half of Samsung Foundry's 4nm capacity is now earmarked for HBM4 base dies, with some estimating the share at 50% to 60%, though Samsung has not disclosed exact figures.

The outgoing generation stays on 4nm: the M2700 for the 2027 Galaxy S27 adopts optical shrink for about 4% area reduction, steps 3GPP support from Release 17 to Release 18, and adds enhanced non-terrestrial network (NTN) capability.

Chinese chip-substrate maker Xinai Technology (芯爱科技) has closed an A2 financing round of nearly 1.5 billion yuan, with strategic investors including Victory Giant Technology and Rockchip, Jiangsu provincial and municipal state-owned funds, continued backing from existing shareholders such as Wuhan Yuefeng, and China Renaissance Securities as sole financial advisor.

The company says total social-capital backing now exceeds 5 billion yuan, including over 3 billion yuan of equity financing raised over five years, plus more than 200 million yuan paid in by employees from their own funds.

Its products — FCBGA, FCCSP and Coreless ETS substrates — target AI cloud, edge and device applications; the production line went live in May 2023, passed certification with JCET, Huatian and Tongfu within seven months of sampling, and entered ASE's system within ten months, qualifying with ASE and SPIL for volume production and covering the world's top-ten OSATs outside the US.

On process, 5-micron line/space has passed technical validation, 7-micron is sampling with key customers and 8-micron is in stable mass production; substrates for 2nm nodes are expected in mass production within 2026, with capacity tilted toward 6/4/3nm nodes.

The round funds high-end FCBGA capacity expansion, glass-substrate R&D and co-development of domestic core materials; the company is building a 415-mu base with total investment over 10 billion yuan, with the P2 plant expected online in May 2027 and P3 breaking ground in 2027 for a 2028 ramp. Morgan Stanley research cited in the report sees global high-end substrates roughly balanced in 2026 but in sustained shortage from 2027, widening through 2030 — though Xinai concedes it still trails Ibiden and Samsung Electro-Mechanics in scale and in-house high-end materials.
title: Xinai Technology Raises Nearly ¥1.5B A2 Round to Expand High-End Chip Substrates

body: South Korea's LX Semicon is exiting the silicon carbide business and selling more than 60 patents covering SiC devices and epitaxial wafers, with a domestic Korean power-semiconductor company selected as preferred bidder, according to THE ELEC on October 14.

The whole patent portfolio is offered as a package — not piecemeal — at an expected price below 1 billion won (about 5.013 million yuan); the MOSFET patents cover planar and trench gate structures, with filings in Korea, the US, China, Europe, Japan and Taiwan and protection running to 2045.

LX Semicon entered SiC in 2021 by acquiring LG Innotek's device-manufacturing equipment and patents — a project that had run as a national program since 2019 — but strategy shifted after Lee Yoon-tae became CEO at end-2023: the SiC R&D unit was downsized in 2024 and its joint venture with Japan's Sanken Electric was liquidated in the first half of this year.

The retreat comes as annual sales fell for three straight years, from 2.1193 trillion won in 2022 to a projected 1.6391 trillion won in 2025; first-half 2026 revenue dropped 7.6% year on year to 789.9 billion won and operating profit fell 39% to 42.6 billion won, with display-driver ICs still accounting for over 86% of revenue.

body: Sipeed (矽速科技) has launched the SLogic32U3, billed as the world's first portable logic analyzer with a USB3.2 Gen2 (10Gbps) Type-C interface — the third generation of its SLogic line.

At its core is Gowin Semiconductor's GW5AT-LV60UG225C2/I1 FPGA from the Arora-V family, built on a 22nm SRAM process, with four 12.5Gbps SERDES lanes, native PCIe 3.0, 10GbE and USB3.2 support, and Gowin's single-chip USB3.x controller-plus-PHY IP that removes the need for an external USB3 PHY.

The analyzer offers 32 digital acquisition channels — 1400MS/s in 4-channel mode and 200MS/s with all 32 channels active — plus 2Gbit of onboard DDR3 buffering, with waveform data streamed directly to host memory and disk so sampling depth is no longer limited by local hardware cache.

It features adjustable thresholds, Sigrok open-source ecosystem compatibility, an expandable ADC analog-acquisition module and a CNC-machined aluminum body, targeting embedded development, bus-protocol debugging and hardware reverse engineering; Gowin also released a DK_USB_GW5AT LV60UG225 evaluation platform with Type-C for developers.

body: The sixth RISC-V China Summit, held October 19, framed 2026 as a milestone year for the architecture, with speakers pointing to a one-new-chip-generation-per-year cadence and a move into high-performance, cloud and AI-native computing.

Server-chip startup 进迭时空 debuted the V100: 46 cores (six XiangShan "Kunminghu" high-performance cores plus 40 in-house efficiency cores), eight DDR5 channels and 52 PCIe 5.0 lanes, fully compliant with the RISC-V server-class RVA23 specification after three years of development — alongside joint compute, AI-compute and storage system offerings.

China's RISC-V working committee said the country shipped more than 3 billion RISC-V chips in 2025 — roughly half the global total, making it the largest single market — with an output value (chips, modules and systems) of about 170 billion yuan, and 476 OpenHarmony product certifications covering 30-plus RISC-V MCUs.

Other signals included Europe's Open Chip project taping out the Bear 10 sample — described as Europe's first sub-2nm server chip — in under two years, RISC-V International chief architect Krste Asanović confirming the CLRB-M microcontroller and RVA23 profiles for production in 2026, and Tenstorrent reporting roughly 750,000 RISC-V elements deployed at scale.

NVIDIA's Vera CPU Wins Modal as First Major Customer, Aims at $20B FY Sales
body: AI cloud startup Modal announced on October 19 that it will deploy NVIDIA's Vera CPUs to host AI agents, in what eet-china described as the chip's first major customer win. Early testing shows Vera doubles the number of tasks an AI agent can complete.

Modal previously ran entirely on Intel and AMD chips and will now move to a hybrid deployment. Vera, unveiled at GTC on March 16, packs 88 in-house Olympus cores with per-core simultaneous multithreading, plus a second-generation LPDDR5X memory subsystem delivering up to 1.2TB/s of bandwidth; NVIDIA claims twice the processing efficiency and 50% faster speed than traditional CPUs, and the chip is in full production.

NVIDIA expects Vera sales of at least $20 billion in the current fiscal year (ending January 2027), with a long-term addressable market of about $200 billion. Cloud partners include Alibaba Cloud, ByteDance, CoreWeave, Lambda, Nebius, Nscale and Oracle Cloud Infrastructure; OpenAI, Anthropic, Oracle and Perplexity also plan to adopt it.
Separately, Modal said on October 14 it closed a $750 million Series D led by Accel at a $15.75 billion post-money valuation, with annualized revenue run-rate exceeding $1 billion.

title: Samsung Plans 2027 Entry Into Silicon Photonics Foundry, Eyes Full CPO by 2029
body: Samsung plans to enter silicon photonics in 2027, starting with 12-inch wafer foundry services for photonic integrated circuits and later expanding into optoelectronic integration and optical packaging, South Korea's MTN reported on October 16. The company is also considering acquisitions to fill out its technology portfolio.

The roadmap calls for a thermocompression-bonded optical engine in 2027, hybrid copper bonding in 2028, and a complete co-packaged optics (CPO) offering in 2029. Samsung first disclosed its silicon photonics foundry ambitions at OFC in March 2026, showing a 300mm-wafer PDK whose silicon modulator was independently verified by imec at 224Gbps per channel — enough for 800G (4-channel) or 1.6T (8-channel) optical modules.

Samsung has reportedly purchased probe stations from FormFactor and MPI to build in-house photonics wafer test capability and has secured an order from a major optical transceiver module maker. Yole Group forecasts the optical transceiver market growing from about $10 billion in 2021 to $112 billion in 2031, a CAGR of roughly 35%.

The foundry contest remains lopsided: TrendForce put TSMC's share of top-ten foundry revenue at 72.5% in Q2 2026 versus 5.9% for Samsung, whose COUPE platform is seen as the CPO ecosystem reference. GlobalFoundries bought Singapore's Advanced Micro Foundry in November 2025 to become the largest pure-play silicon photonics foundry by revenue, while UMC licensed imec's iSiPP in December 2025.

title: Alibaba's T-Head XuanTie Surpasses 6 Billion RISC-V Cores Shipped
body: DAMO Academy's XuanTie (T-Head) said its cumulative RISC-V chip shipments have exceeded 6 billion units, spanning smart devices and server-adjacent applications, in a story carried by eefocus on October 20.

Its flagship C950, released in March 2026, runs at 3.2GHz and scores over 70 in single-core SPECint2006 — above 22 points per GHz — a record for RISC-V. Through the XT-LINK multicore interconnect, C950 achieves over 75% linear scaling. The team claims more than 10% performance advantages over mainstream incumbent architectures on four types of agentic AI workloads.

At the 2026 RISC-V China Summit in Shenzhen, XuanTie launched the automotive-enhanced E908A IP — the industry's first RISC-V CPU IP meeting both ASIL-B and ASIL-D, with single-point fault metric (SPFM) above 90% — and outlined the C950A, an automotive version targeting five times the performance of existing automotive RISC-V products, expected by the end of 2027.

Ecosystem momentum: the team is the second-largest contributor to GCC's RISC-V code globally and contributed more than half of OpenJDK's RISC-V code; DAMO expert Li Chunqiang said simultaneous multithreading is yielding 30% interim performance gains, with single-core multithreaded SPECint2006 targeted to exceed 100 points by 2028. SHD Research estimates automotive RISC-V SoC revenue at $1.84 billion in 2025, rising to $12.3 billion in 2031 at a 37.3% CAGR.

title: Samsung Electro-Mechanics Signs 360.5 Billion Won Package Substrate Supply Deal
body: Samsung Electro-Mechanics disclosed in a regulatory filing on October 19 that it has signed a 360.5 billion won (about $250 million) contract with a global major to supply semiconductor package substrates for storage devices. It is the company's first disclosed long-term agreement (LTA) in the package substrate segment, according to laoyaoba.

The deal brings Samsung Electro-Mechanics' disclosed LTAs this year to seven — the rest concentrated in components such as silicon capacitors, MLCCs and inductors — with cumulative contracted value of roughly 4.3 trillion won.

The company produces FC-BGA and BGA substrates through its package solutions division; industry observers attribute the deal to growing demand for high-value AI server GPU/CPU substrates and chiplet-based heterogeneous integration.

Last month the company unveiled investment plans of 4.27 trillion won for its FC-BGA facility in Sejong, South Korea and 2.51 trillion won for manufacturing equipment in Vietnam; including the Vietnam plant expansion, total spending is expected to exceed 8 trillion won.

title: Dry Descum Duopoly: Lam Holds 40%, China's ACM at 33.7%, Says Jiwei Report
body: 集微咨询 (Jiwei Consulting) released its 2026 descum-equipment industry report on October 20, pegging the global dry descum equipment market at about $858 million in 2025 and forecasting $1.471 billion by 2032, a CAGR of roughly 8.01%.
The market is a duopoly: CR5 exceeds 90%, with Lam Research leading at 40% and China's ACM Research (屹唐股份) close behind at 33.7%, followed by TEL (15%), PSK (7%) and Hitachi High-Tech (4.3%).

China's descum equipment market (dry plus wet tools) reached about 4.73 billion yuan in 2025, up 18.6% year on year, driven by continued capex from SMIC, Hua Hong, YMTC and CXMT. The domestic-content rate for new dry descum tools on 28nm-and-above lines now exceeds 80%, and ACM's products are in use at global top-ten chipmakers.
Demand intensity rises with process complexity: per-wafer descum cycles grow from about 30 at 28nm to around 70 at 3nm logic, while 3D NAND stacks move from 128 layers toward 300-plus.

title: South Korean Finance Minister Sees Chip Boom Lasting Through 2027; Maeil Warns of 2029 Memory "Red Ocean"
body: South Korea's Minister of Economy and Finance Lee Hyoung-il said on October 17, on the sidelines of the IMF–World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok, that the semiconductor boom would last "at least until next year," citing a still-wide gap between supply and demand as supply continues to expand.

SK hynix's second-quarter operating profit surged 557% year on year, and management reiterated that demand will outstrip supply through 2030; CEO Kwak Noh-jung said in August that the memory shortage would persist into 2030. Over the past year, Samsung Electronics shares rose roughly 150% and SK hynix about 250%.

Volatility remains sharp: on October 13 Samsung fell 7.5% intraday to 231,750 won and SK hynix dropped 8.4% as the KOSPI lost nearly 7% to 5,944.31 points, and on October 15 the index plunged 7.57% in a single session. Elon Musk responded on X that China "will produce a lot of RAM in 2028."

South Korea's Maeil Business Newspaper argued in an October 15 column that the period through 2028 is a "safe zone," but warned that new capacity flooding the market from 2029 onward means a memory "red ocean in 2029" and a downturn in 2030. SK hynix reports third-quarter results on October 28 and Samsung on October 29; US September CPI rose 3.7% year on year.

title: Report: Samsung to Use TSMC 3nm for NVIDIA's Custom NVHBM Base Die
body: South Korea's Seoul Economic Daily reported on October 18 that Samsung Electronics will outsource the base die at the bottom of NVIDIA's custom HBM, "NVHBM," to TSMC on its 3nm process. NVIDIA unveiled NVHBM on August 26, 2026; its key design move is relocating the GPU's (which NVIDIA calls XPU) memory controller into the HBM stack's base die alongside an in-house PHY.

Per the report, NVIDIA requires all three suppliers — Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron — to build the base die on TSMC 3nm while the core die uses sixth-generation 1c DRAM. UBS estimates 2027 HBM demand will grow 91% year-on-year to about 615 billion Gb against only around 546 billion Gb of new supply, leaving a roughly 10% shortfall. Samsung is separately validating base-die production on its own 2nm process.

Caveat: as of publication, NVIDIA, Samsung, TSMC, SK Hynix and Micron had issued no official statements; all details trace to the newspaper's anonymous industry sources. SK Hynix previously held the lead NVIDIA HBM supplier position on the strength of its early base-die work.

title: Zhongxingwei Launches 12 Production Interconnect Chips, China's First PCIe 6.0 Switch
body: At its October 15 "brand and full-stack product" launch in Wuxi, Chinese interconnect chipmaker Zhongxingwei (众星微) unveiled 12 already-mass-produced high-performance interconnect chips with supporting core IP, plus three next-generation products: a PCIe 6.0 switch, an 800G multi-protocol AI NIC, and a multi-mode RAID chip.

The company frames the AI compute bottleneck as "transport capacity": in large-model training, cluster compute utilization runs as low as just over 20% and at most 53%, while interconnect chips account for 8–9% of system value in GB300- and VR200-class super-nodes. China's first all-domestic 100,000-card compute cluster adopted six Zhongxingwei chips, deploying roughly 200,000 units, with an in-house 32T InfiniBand switch chip paired with 400G NICs handling intra-cluster traffic.

New products include China's first PCIe 6.0 144-lane switch, with native fabric for high-speed XPU interconnect and CXL 3.1 for memory pooling, and a new multi-mode RAID chip whose core throughput is double that of mainstream international rivals. Its storage-interconnect lines (HBA/RAID/SAS Expander) benchmark against overseas leaders across 50 typical workloads.

On quality: 500 servers and 1,000 boards ran 600,000 hours of continuous on-machine testing; chip customer return rates are below 100 DPPM and board returns below 500 DPPM. Ecosystem coverage spans 15+ cloud platforms, 50+ OS variants, 300+ optical-module models and 7 mainstream CPU platforms.

title: Fulin Integrated Raises Nearly ¥1B Series B to Expand InP/GaAs Foundry for AI Optical Modules
body: Putian, Fujian-based compound-semiconductor foundry Fulin Integrated (福联集成, founded 2015) has closed a Series B round of nearly 1 billion yuan, co-led by Shenzhen Capital Group (深创投) and Industrial Securities' investment arm, with Fujian Electronics & Information Group, SMIC Fortune (中芯聚源), a national-level industry fund and others participating. Proceeds will fund phase-two expansion, lifting capacity by more than 50%; the company says it is currently sold out at full utilization.

The round's core draw is its 4-inch indium phosphide (InP) line for optical chips: it has entered the supply chains of the world's top-three optical module makers, serving 800G and next-generation 1.6T modules. Its other line is 6-inch gallium arsenide for RF chips — handset power amplifiers, Wi-Fi front ends, satellite communications — serving tier-one customers at home and abroad.

Market context cited in the coverage: global InP substrate shipments are estimated at about 910,000 wafers in 2025 rising to about 1.28 million in 2027, and Lumentum forecasts an 85% CAGR in AI-driven InP optical-channel shipments. In GaAs foundry, Taiwan's WIN Semiconductors holds over 60% of the merchant market at 43,000 wafers a month, while Sanan IC is China's largest at 18,000 a month; Wi-Fi 7 is lifting PA content per handset from 3–4 to 8–10 units.

The company is listed among Fujian's key IPO-candidate cultivation enterprises, and data from Cailian Press cited in the article puts the probability of follow-on financing within two years at around 77%, signaling clear IPO intent.

title: Changfei Advanced Discloses Diffusion-Bonded SiC Modules, A3-Grade Fab at Baychip Expo
body: At the 2026 Bay Area Semiconductor Industry Ecosystem Expo (Baychip Expo) in Shenzhen, SiC power semiconductor maker Changfei Advanced disclosed fresh progress on high-performance SiC MOSFETs, PCB-embedded packaging and its A3-grade wafer fab, in an interview with Li Gangqun, vice president of its strategic operations center.

The EZ family is China's first power module line built on an advanced diffusion-bonding process, targeting AI data centers (AIDC) and solid-state transformers (SST). Diffusion-bonded joints deliver 2–3x higher bonding strength; the EZ2C cuts junction-to-case thermal resistance by 18% and full-load die junction temperature by more than 25°C, while supporting operation above 200°C. The EZ3C uses an efficient SHB three-level topology to push a single SST module above 100 kW, halving the cascade stages of a 10 kV AI SST system from 16 to 8.

On trench devices, the company started its trench MOSFET patent program in 2023; double-side deep masking/burial techniques plus rounded trench-bottom processing cut trench sidewall roughness (Ra) to 0.15 nm versus 0.7 nm for rivals. As of October 2025 it held 79 public patents in the field, ranking third worldwide; first- and second-generation devices are designated TG1N and TG2N.

Its Wuhan base is the first SiC wafer fab in China to deploy an A3-grade AMHS overhead-transport and dispatch system, with an automatic wafer-start rate above 98% and smart dispatch above 90%. CP yield on 5 mm × 5 mm automotive-grade large dice is stable above 98%, new-product tape-in cycles are 3x faster, and an AI-driven fab utilities system cut overall fab energy use by more than 10.5%.

title: Zhiyuan Robotics Takes Strategic Stake in Tsinghua-Backed RISC-V AI Chip Startup
body: Embodied-intelligence leader Zhiyuan Robotics has taken a strategic stake in Xinji Wuxian (芯际无限), the only RISC-V AI chip company incubated with technology transfer and equity from Tsinghua University. Founded in August 2023, the startup covers the full humanoid-robot stack, from end-effector and motion control to cerebellum and brain-level decision chips.

Its XC64AE series is purpose-built for embodied-intelligence scenarios, with the second-generation XC64AE family slated to complete tape-out in 2027. On the automotive side, the XC32MC body-motor-control MCU is already in mass production in vehicles with aggregate orders exceeding 5 million units; the XC32LS meets the ASIL-D functional-safety grade, recently taped out and powered on, and is now in testing with multiple automakers and Tier-1 suppliers ahead of 2027 mass production; the XC32DC central domain controller integrates an in-house NPU.

The coverage notes that traditional ARM-based automotive chips can carry combined licensing costs of 15–20% of product cost, and that Tsinghua Huakong Technology Transfer Co. took a strategic stake in 2026 via core RISC-V IP. The team is led by founder and CEO Cheng Baozhong and CTO Wei Jian — formerly of Qualcomm, where he led the first in-house GPU and taped out ASIL-D RISC-V cores and automotive cockpit chips.
Zhiyuan, backed by investors including Huawei and Tencent, began its Hong Kong IPO process in July with a targeted valuation of 40–50 billion yuan.

title: Dell CEO Warns AI Server Memory Shortage to Worsen Into 2027
body: Dell Technologies CEO Michael Dell has warned that tight supply of HBM and DRAM will worsen further in 2027, as AI infrastructure demand keeps outpacing global memory capacity growth — making memory the key bottleneck for the AI server industry.
Dell currently sits on a record $95 billion backlog of enterprise and AI server orders, but converting those orders into revenue hinges on securing enough memory chips.

According to The Wall Street Journal, Dell believes the supply constraint could last up to four years, since new fabs take years from planning to full production — much of the added capacity is not expected to be fully online until 2029 or 2030.

To limit risk, Dell runs a lean-inventory model — buying DRAM close to final assembly to avoid tying up working capital — while locking in supply through long-term vendor agreements and customer prepayments.
Rising memory prices are also pushing up manufacturing costs for AI servers and other high-end systems, adding pressure across the AI supply chain.

title: XHEART Closes Strategic Round, Lifetime Funding Reaches ~5 Billion Yuan
body: Chinese physical-AI compute chip startup XHEART (新芯航途) completed a strategic funding round on October 16, bringing its cumulative financing to approximately 5 billion yuan.
Renault Group joined as a first-time investor, Chery Auto increased its stake, and domestic memory leader CXMT (Changxin Memory) also participated in the round.

XHEART builds dedicated compute for edge-side physical-AI models. Its flagship product, the X7 ADAS large-model chip launched in March, uses a dedicated NPU with a hardware-software co-design architecture targeting 200+ TOPS for L2++ urban driving assistance and L3/L4 autonomous driving.

The X7 debuted on the SAIC Volkswagen ID.ERA 9X and is entering the supply systems of SAIC's MG and Roewe brands, GM's Cadillac, and selected Chery models. The company's largest shareholder traces back to Momenta founder Cao Xudong.

title: VTest Wins Approval for 2 Billion Yuan Convertible Bond to Expand High-End Chip Test Capacity
body: Shanghai VTest Semiconductor (伟测科技) has received SSE approval to issue up to 2 billion yuan in convertible bonds, with proceeds earmarked for expanding test capacity for AI compute chips, memory chips, and high-end CIS.

The funds target two projects: the Shanghai HQ base (700 million yuan of the raise) and the Southwest HQ and R&D test base in Chengdu (800 million yuan), both involving new land, facilities, and high-end test equipment.

VTest, a leading third-party IC test house, covers wafer test, final test, SLT, and burn-in for AI chips, CPUs, GPUs, DPUs, SoCs, FPGAs, MCUs, memory, RF, and high-end CIS devices, serving over 200 customers including Unisoc, ZTE Microelectronics, GigaDevice, Fudan Microelectronics, SMIC, Rockchip, and Novosense.

The company reported H1 2026 revenue of 1.072 billion yuan, up 69% year on year, with net profit of 159 million yuan, up 57.6%, driven by high-end test demand from AI compute, smart driving, and large-capacity memory chips.
This is VTest's second straight year of convertible-bond financing, following an 1.175 billion yuan issue in April 2025 that was redeemed in March 2026 after a share-price rally.

title: Jialichuang Plans Hong Kong Listing Less Than Three Months After A-Share Debut
body: Jialichuang (嘉立创, 001232) announced plans to issue H shares and list on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange main board — less than three months after its A-share debut on August 4, when its shares peaked above 234 yuan and market value once exceeded 130 billion yuan.

The company, a one-stop electronics-industry service provider covering PCB manufacturing, electronic component distribution, and assembly, says the listing would support its globalization strategy, widen offshore financing channels, and strengthen its overseas brand.

Overseas revenue grew 63.76% year on year to 1.516 billion yuan in H1 2026, accounting for 21.14% of total revenue. The company also guided Q1–Q3 2026 net profit to rise 78.76%–118.48% year on year, partly on overseas growth.
In the same roundup, Dongshan Precision received CSRC filing approval to issue up to 234,038,600 H shares for a Hong Kong listing, moving its IPO process to the HKEX hearing and pricing stage.

title: Changfei Advanced Launches SiC MOSFET Series, New Power Modules at Shenzhen Tech Event
body: SiC power semiconductor maker Changfei Advanced, founded in May 2022, held a "Everest Summit" technology launch in Shenzhen on October 15, unveiling its high-performance SiC MOSFET series PG4E/PG5E/PG6N, E2Drive automotive main-drive power modules, DeepXE embedded-PCB power modules, and EZ2C/3C — described as China's first diffusion-welded SiC power modules — alongside new products for AI data centers, industrial, and consumer markets.

The company said its portfolio has grown from zero to 131 products, with process cell size shrunk from 5.8μm to 2.8μm, a 575-person R&D team, and combined annual capacity of 420,000 SiC wafers across its Wuhan and Wuhu fabs. Wuhan is billed as the SiC industry's first A3-level smart wafer fab, with MOSFET production cycle of about 40 days and over 98% CP yield on 5×5mm chips.

On specs: the 1200V PG4E posts room-temperature Rsp of 2.2 mΩ·cm² (4.4 mΩ·cm² at 175°C), 2.1μs short-circuit withstand (27% above rivals), and 11.2% higher avalanche energy. The PG5E cuts room-temperature Rsp to 1.9 mΩ·cm² (about 13.5% below the prior generation) with 30% better short-circuit withstand versus competitors, while the PG6N reaches 1.7 mΩ·cm² Rsp and supports operation up to 200–225°C.

For modules: the E2Dmini-J, co-developed with Jingwei HiRain, delivers 540 Arms peak current (20% above the 450 Arms industry level) with 36% lower stray inductance. DeepXE's embedded-PCB module gets stray inductance down to 0.9 nH (75% below conventional packaging), 20% higher current density, 15% lower thermal resistance, and halves size and weight — 24 SiC MOSFETs on a poker-card-sized footprint reaching 250 kW peak. The diffusion-welded EZ2C/3C replaces tin-based solder (melting point ~500°C vs 230°C) with 2–3x bond strength and thermal conductivity, cutting case-to-sink thermal resistance by 18% and full-load junction temperature by over 25°C; EZ3C pushes a single SST module from 70 kW to over 100 kW and halves 10 kV AI SST cascade stages from 16 to 8.

Automotive SiC chips now number 50-plus models with over 20 million units shipped at a claimed 0 PPM quality record; consumer products span 38 models (650V–800V) with over 100 million units shipped, and industrial products 93 models (650V–3300V) with 15 million shipped. For data centers, its 800V HVDC lineup targets PSU cabinets of 18 kW/30 kW at over 98.5% efficiency and 40–80 kW SST modules. On the trench-MOS roadmap, the first-generation TG1N (1200V, 11 mΩ) is in mass production; the second generation shrinks cell size 27% and on-resistance 16% (mass production in 2026), with a third generation at 1.5μm cell and 1.3 mΩ·cm² Rsp slated for 2027 — an Incopat search put its 79 trench-MOS public patents (Oct 2024–Oct 2025) third worldwide behind Fuji Electric (139) and Infineon (109). The article cites a 2025 global SiC power semiconductor market of about $2.79 billion, projected to reach $21.58 billion by 2034 at 25.52% CAGR.

title: China's DF1000 AI Chip Adapts 130B-Parameter Model Training Pipeline in 7 Days
body: Domestic AI-chip startup Dongfang Suanxin said its DF1000 processor, launched in July, completed a full bring-up from chip to cluster in a short period and adapted the training pipeline of the Step 130B large model in just 7 days — clarified as getting operators, distributed links, and cluster scheduling working so training could start, not a complete from-scratch training run of the 130B model.

The DF1000 uses a software-defined chip architecture whose compute arrays and interconnect can be dynamically switched between data movement, tensor, and vector compute without a respin, and a 3D hybrid-bonded near-memory compute design with logic and DRAM wafers vertically stacked, copper-to-copper direct bonding, and sub-micron interconnect pitch.

Measured figures: 520 TFLOPS of BF16 compute at 14nm, 6.4 TB/s memory bandwidth, and 900 GB/s scale-up interconnect bandwidth — over 5x the memory bandwidth of a conventional HBM setup at the same capacity. The software stack supports PyTorch, Megatron-LM, vLLM, Triton, Kubernetes, Hugging Face, and SGLang, with LLaMA, DeepSeek, and Qwen models claimed to work out of the box.
VP Guo Wei said at the DF1000 launch that the chip's goal is to fix real bottlenecks in large-model training and inference, not to look good on a few spec parameters.

title: China's FPGA Vendors Push High-End Launches in 2026, Review Says
body: Chinese FPGA vendors are moving from entry-level "drop-in replacements" to original high-end innovation in 2026, according to an October 18 industry review on eefocus, which points to four shifts: Physical AI going mainstream, FPGA Agent intelligent development, Chiplet packaging breakthroughs, and volume ramp of domestic high-end products.

In high-end compute, Pango Microsystems' Titan-3 series is described as China's top mass-produced general FPGA, delivering 1,300K LUTs of logic capacity with DDR5 and PCIe 3.0, targeting 5G/6G communications, data-center acceleration, and high-speed image codecs. For edge AI, Fudan Microelectronics' new AI heterogeneous computing platform combines CPU, FPGA, and an in-house NPU for the edge deployment of 70B-class models, with its FMZQ400TAI part rated at 128 TOPS INT8 peak.

In automotive, Anlogic's Phoenix PH1P series passed AEC-Q100 Grade 2 qualification, among the few domestic high-end FPGAs that can ship in cars in volume. Efinix's 16nm Titanium series pairs a Quantum variable-logic architecture with PCIe Gen4 and 16 Gbps SerDes for low-power, high-speed interconnect such as optical communications and high-speed backplanes.

The review also notes smarter domestic EDA tooling lowering the development barrier: Pango's PDS tool is positioned against Xilinx Vivado with SystemVerilog support, and all major domestic vendors now ship AI-assisted development flows for auto-routing, timing closure, and bug triage.

title: Japan Approves TSMC's 3nm Plan for Kumamoto Fab Two, Targeting 6,000 Wafers a Month
body: Japan's Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry on October 16 approved TSMC's plan to produce 3nm advanced semiconductors at its second Kumamoto fab, which would be the first 3nm chip manufacturing on Japanese soil.

The fab was originally slated for 6nm and 12nm processes at 48,000 wafers per month plus 40nm capacity; the new plan sets 3nm output at 6,000 wafers per month, with METI saying the sharp capacity cut reflects the shift to higher-performance products. The approval covers the fab's first phase, and TSMC plans to add capacity with further government support.
METI also approved changes at the operating first Kumamoto fab: 12–16nm production will be discontinued, and 22–28nm capacity will be trimmed from 55,000 to 45,000 wafers per month.
Japanese media report the switch to 3nm reflects rising AI demand, and Nikkei confirmed the new 3nm plant has been approved for subsidies.

title: Shanghai OSAT Xiangxin Integrated Circuits Declared Bankrupt
body: The Shanghai Third Intermediate People's Court on October 15 declared Shanghai Xiangxin Integrated Circuits Co. bankrupt (case (2025) Hu 03 Po No. 918), ruling the company cannot pay its due debts and its assets are insufficient to cover them; the court had accepted the bankruptcy liquidation application on September 19, 2025.

Founded in November 2011, Xiangxin focused on power-management IC packaging and testing, building SOP and SOT lines covering wafer thinning, dicing, wire bonding, molding, metal surface treatment, trimming and final test, with total investment of RMB 60 million.
Its packaging services supplied chipmakers including Wuxi Chipown, with products going into consumer electronics and industrial control applications.
The ruling adds another bankruptcy case to China's intensely competitive OSAT sector, where many smaller packagers are under pressure.

title: Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan: US-China Chip Gap "Not That Big"
body: In a Tokyo interview in early October, Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan said the US government's minority stake in Intel has no impact on the company's governance and does not affect its commercial strategy, and that Intel's restructuring is 80% complete.
He credited government backing for enabling long-term investment in a competitive foundry business, citing TSMC's decade-plus journey to chipmaking leadership.

On China's semiconductor progress, Tan said US and Chinese firms "each have their own strengths and weaknesses," and when asked whether Chinese chipmaking could catch up within five to ten years, replied: "as things stand, I don't think the gap is that big."

title: Huawei: 2027 Kirin Chip in Testing, Results "As Expected"
body: At a Kirin chip technology briefing at Huawei's Shanghai Lianqihu R&D center on October 13 — its first dedicated Kirin event in six years — Huawei said it systematically reviewed the mass-production progress of its "logic folding" technology.
The company also disclosed that its next-generation Kirin chip, expected in 2027, has entered testing, with results meeting expectations.

title: China's Equipment Trio Rushes Into Hybrid Bonding: Tuojing's RMB 2.5 Billion Deal Leads
body: On the evening of October 15, Tuojing Technology and NAURA both disclosed acquisition plans targeting hybrid bonding equipment; three days earlier, AMEC's subsidiary announced a capital injection of up to RMB 35 million into bonding firm Qinghe Jingyuan — three major domestic chip-equipment makers moving on the same track within days.

Tuojing Technology plans to acquire 82.97% of Wuxi Shangji plus 100% each of Wuxi Kuanghang and Shanghai Tainawei for RMB 2.5 billion via shares and cash, raising up to RMB 1.82 billion in supporting funds alongside. Wuxi Shangji, a PVD and etching equipment maker, committed to revenues of no less than RMB 350 million, 450 million and 610 million for 2026–2028. After the deal, Tuojing will offer a complete 3D-integration equipment product line covering thin-film deposition, etching, bonding and metrology, enabling one-stop procurement and joint process development for customers.

NAURA's subsidiary will acquire hybrid-bonding equipment maker Nuohe Jianwei for RMB 405 million in cash. Nuohe's tools have already reached nanometer-level alignment precision, secured repeat orders, and are awaiting validation by leading customers.

Hybrid bonding, called the "chokepoint process" of 3D chips, is entering a fast landing phase, with related equipment demand expected to multiply by 2030, driven by the explosive growth of AI/HPC and HBM. Dutch firm BESI still holds about 70% of the global market, but Chinese equipment makers are accelerating their catch-up from zero to one, shifting competition from single-tool breakthroughs to platform-based turnkey solutions.

title: Galaxy Microelectronics to Acquire Hengtaike for RMB 645 Million in Power-Device Push
body: Galaxy Microelectronics (688689.SH) announced after market close on October 16 that it plans to acquire 100% of Hengtaike Semiconductor (Shanghai) for RMB 645 million through share issuance, and will raise supporting funds of up to RMB 580.5 million for the industrialization of high-reliability medium/high-voltage MOS device packaging projects.

The deal values the transaction at RMB 28.24 per share, involving about 22.84 million new shares. Hengtaike is a national-level "Little Giant" company specializing in power semiconductor products for construction machinery, drones, photovoltaics and energy storage, with industry-leading medium-voltage SGT MOSFET and high-voltage Super Junction technology.

In the 150V–200V range, Hengtaike's medium/high-voltage SGT MOSFETs are said to match the product lines of international leading vendors. The transaction values Hengtaike's equity at RMB 586 million under the income approach, a 139.63% premium.

Galaxy Microelectronics, which focuses on semiconductor discrete devices with an IDM model, concentrates its power-device portfolio in the low-voltage segment. The acquisition aims to quickly fill its medium/high-voltage gap and accelerate the iteration of automotive-grade devices and new product launches, following the company's September announcement of a RMB 1.078 billion capacity expansion project.

title: Xingfu Electronic to Raise Up to RMB 260 Million for 40,000-Ton Semiconductor-Grade Phosphoric Acid Project
body: Xingfu Electronic (688545.SH) announced it plans to issue shares under a simplified procedure to raise no more than RMB 260 million, with the net proceeds fully funding a 40,000-ton-per-year electronic-grade phosphoric acid project; total project investment is RMB 480 million.
The move is aimed at consolidating its leading position in electronic-grade phosphoric acid, a key wet-chemical material used in chip manufacturing.

title: Fujian Huaqing Takes China's No.1 and World's No.2 Spot in Aluminum Nitride Ceramic Substrates
body: According to YHResearch's "Global Aluminum Nitride (AlN) Ceramic Substrate Market Report 2025-2031", Fujian Huaqing Electronic Materials Technology Co., Ltd. has surpassed several established international giants to rank first in China and second globally by AlN ceramic substrate market share.

AlN ceramics are a core base material for the power semiconductor industry — prized for high thermal conductivity, high temperature tolerance, high resistivity and low dielectric loss — serving as key heat-dissipation and packaging substrates for IGBTs and large-scale integrated circuits across 5G communications, photovoltaics, energy storage, rail transit and automotive electronics.

The company, a national "Little Giant" firm and China's first professional high-thermal-conductivity AlN ceramics manufacturer, attributes the breakthrough to in-house high-purity ceramic powder synthesis — ending dependence on imported premium powders — plus full-chain processes from tape casting and high-temperature sintering to precision grinding and etching, solving the industry's high-end AlN mass-production challenge.

Its products cover powder, substrates, copper-clad laminates and precision ceramic structural parts, and have won recognition from leading customers upstream and downstream worldwide, marking another domestic substitution milestone in a long-overseas-dominated key material.

title: SEMI Sees 300mm Fab Equipment Spending Hitting US$227 Billion by 2029
body: SEMI's 300mm Fab Outlook report forecasts global 300mm front-end fab equipment spending at US$149 billion in 2026, up 31% year on year, staying in double-digit growth to reach US$227 billion by 2029. Americas-region investment is projected to climb from US$18.1 billion in 2026 to US$40.6 billion in 2029.

IDC data shows Nvidia's share of China's data-center AI chip market fell to 34% in the first half of 2026, with shipments of 678,000 accelerators, down 44% year on year. Huawei shipped 572,000 AI accelerators, up roughly 90%, taking 28% of the market. Of the 11 Chinese chipmakers IDC tracks, nine grew shipments year on year; total China AI accelerator shipments reached 2.008 million units, and IDC expects 19% growth for the full year.

Counterpoint Research's preliminary data shows global Q3 smartphone shipments down 20% year on year — a 14-year Q3 low — as rising DRAM and NAND prices pushed up retail prices by 20% this year. Samsung held 23% share to stay number one, while Apple reached 22%, its first time above 20% in a third quarter.

Wuxi-based Zhongxingwei, a relatively low-profile domestic interconnect chipmaker that has spent six years on the segment, held a brand and full-stack product launch where it presented its full-scenario high-performance interconnect chip platform for the first time.

The lineup spans general-compute interconnect — HBA cards, RAID cards, RoCE NICs and PCIe switch chips for server and storage systems — and AI-compute interconnect, including PCIe switches, 400G InfiniBand NICs and IB switches. The company also launched three self-developed new chips: the C82-4G, described as China's first PCIe 6.0 switch (up to 144 lanes at 64 GT/s per lane, doubling PCIe 5.0 bandwidth), an 800G multi-protocol AI NIC, also described as a domestic first, and a multi-mode RAID chip supporting SAS, SATA and PCIe 5.0 with a built-in hardware encryption engine.

Zhongxingwei says cumulative shipments have exceeded 800,000 units, with over 400,000 units shipped in 2025 alone and revenue surpassing 1 billion yuan. Its products are in use at Inspur, Lenovo, H3C and ZTE, and it signed strategic cooperation agreements with seven industry partners — Kylinsoft, UnionTech, Tencent Cloud, Inspur, H3C, ZTE and Lenovo.
title: Chinese Interconnect Chipmaker Zhongxingwei Unveils Full-Stack Platform, Tops 800,000 Units Shipped

body: At CIIF 2026, Chinese chipmaker Axera launched the AX8860 series of large-compute edge AI SoCs, targeting industrial intelligence as AI moves from the cloud to the physical world. The series includes the AX8860 and AX8860P, positioned as compute platforms 'born for physical AI.'

Built on a 6nm process after 15 months of development, the chips deliver up to 256 TOPS with mixed-precision compute and are among the industry's first edge chips natively supporting FP4 precision. Each chip carries 273 GB/s of memory bandwidth and natively supports 128GB of LPDDR5X; a built-in AXLink chip-to-chip interface enables dual- and quad-chip cascading with memory pooling, reaching 512GB of memory with four chips — enough to run models above 100 billion parameters, such as DeepSeek V4 Flash, at the edge.

Axera says early AX8860P tests show prefill and decode speeds matching leading international flagship GPUs, while full-load power consumption is only 45% of the competitor's, with multi-chip cascading efficiency holding around 80%. The launch is accompanied by four hardware forms: the A256S core module, PCIe inference cards (single, dual and quad-chip; the quad-chip card offers roughly 1000 TOPS and a 512GB memory pool), the Agentic Box, and edge inference servers.
title: Axera Launches AX8860 Edge AI SoC Series for Industrial 'Physical AI'

body: Chinese RISC-V server-chip startup Ruisixin has closed a new funding round with Renjun Capital and Shuimu Fund participating, according to a report (amount undisclosed). The team comes from the original Berkeley RISC-V project group, and founder Tan Zhangxi studied under RISC-V co-founder David Patterson.

The round caps a dense financing streak across the sector: Lanxin Computing closed a Series B of nearly 2 billion yuan with 18 investors last month, Lingrui Zhixin raised several hundred million yuan in July, and last year Jindie Shikong, Chaorui Technology and Yuefang Technology each closed nine-figure rounds. Overseas, Tenstorrent raised a $693 million Series D.

Policy support is also crystallizing: the 15th Five-Year Plan for electronic information manufacturing issued by MIIT and NDRC lists 'advancing 5th-generation RISC (RISC-V) R&D and industrialization' — the first time RISC-V has appeared as a task item in a national five-year plan. The article notes industry-wide consolidation may be next, as competition shifts from single demos to ecosystem completeness and real deployments.
title: RISC-V Funding Wave: Ruisixin Closes New Round as Sector Eyes Consolidation

body: Chinese AI cloud-compute chip startup Suanmiao Technology announced it has closed its Pre-A2 and A funding rounds, bringing its total fundraising over the past year to nearly 2 billion yuan, according to the report.

The company focuses on R&D and volume production of large-compute AI cloud chips built on a 3D architecture. It says proceeds are earmarked for three priorities: recruiting top R&D talent, doubling down on core-technology iteration, and accelerating the mass-production ramp of its self-developed 3D TokenPU large-model compute chip.
Rather than following the conventional GPU route, Suanmiao is betting its 3D chip architecture can carve out a differentiated path in AI inference compute.
title: 3D-Architecture AI Chip Startup Suanmiao Raises Nearly 2 Billion Yuan in a Year
